title: Waves Adventure 2: Superposition, interference and diffraction
welcome_lead: Today you'll interfere waves through Young's double slit.
meta_desc: IBDP Physics — superposition, constructive/destructive interference, Young's double slit, diffraction.
final_note: You learned waves superpose (add algebraically), constructive at Δd = nλ, destructive at Δd = (n+½)λ, Young's slits give fringes ax/D = λ.

walkthroughs.body_html:
When two waves meet, their displacements add.

Same phase → constructive (loud, bright).
Opposite phase → destructive (silent, dark).

Sources must be coherent (same f, fixed phase relationship).

Light through 2 slits + screen → bright/dark fringes.

Bright (max): path difference Δd = nλ (n = 0, 1, 2, …).
Dark (min): Δd = (n + ½)λ.

Fringe spacing: s = λD/a
where D = slit-screen distance, a = slit separation.

Confirmed wave nature of light (Young, 1801).

Waves spread when they pass through apertures of size ~λ.

Single slit diffraction: minima at sinθ = nλ/b (b = slit width).

Diffraction grating with N slits: maxima at nλ = d sinθ (d = slit spacing).

Sharp, well-spaced — used in spectroscopy.
